✍️ Exam Writing Guide

How to structure every answer by its marks — study this once, apply it everywhere.

This is the single writing-strategy reference for the whole question bank. The individual answers below contain only the exam-ready academic content; use this guide to decide how to present it on paper.

11–2 Mark Answers

Keep them crisp and direct — 1–3 lines (15–70 words).

  • Start with the key term or definition in the very first line.
  • Add one supporting fact, name or example and stop.
  • Never open with background or a full paragraph — the mark is for the point, not the story.

23–5 Mark Answers

A small structured answer, ¾–1¼ pages (70–230 words).

  • Open with a one-line definition, then explain the concept briefly.
  • Add 2–4 points, each as point + explanation, not point only.
  • Include an example only if it directly helps; close with one summary line.

36–8 Mark Answers

Develop through sections, 1¼–2½ pages (220–430 words).

  • Use headings: Definition → Explanation → Components/Features → Example → Conclusion.
  • Fix each important point with a short explanation and, where useful, an example.
  • Add a diagram or code block when the concept is visual or technical.

49–10 Mark Answers

Full teaching-quality treatment, 2–3½ pages (380–600 words).

  • Build basic → advanced: intro → definition → working → components → example → advantages → limitations → applications → conclusion.
  • Explain concepts — never produce bare bullet lists at this length.
  • Programming questions need aim, steps, code, important-line notes and sample output.

512–14 Mark Answers

Comprehensive university answer, 3–5+ pages (650–900+ words).

  • Use multiple academic sections chosen for the question — not every heading blindly.
  • Prefer point + explanation + example/impact everywhere depth is required.
  • Always close with a conclusion and, where relevant, a comparison table or diagram.

6Headings & Structure

Headings turn a block of text into a mark-friendly answer.

  • Use a heading for each distinct idea (Definition, Features, Example…).
  • Underline headings or number them (1. 2. 3.) — examiners tick what they can find.
  • Begin a new paragraph for each new point; keep one idea per point.

7Diagrams & Flow

A labelled diagram earns marks paragraphs cannot.

  • Draw for architecture, process, lifecycle, hierarchy or system design.
  • Keep it simple and label every box and arrow, then briefly explain it below.
  • For MongoDB/React/Angular, a small flow (e.g. Component → Virtual DOM → Real DOM) always fits.

8Presenting Code

Method marks come from the code, not from describing it.

  • Write aim → steps → program → explanation → output in order.
  • Comment key statements or explain them in the line below.
  • For queries, show the collection before and after the command.

9Keywords

Examiners scan for the syllabus vocabulary.

  • Use exact terms (BSON, Virtual DOM, $routeProvider) as they appear in the source.
  • Write each keyword in context once, in bold or underlined.
  • A keyword list alone is not an answer — every keyword must be attached to an explanation.

10Avoid Filler

Longer does not mean repetitive.

  • Never rewrite the same point in different words.
  • No openings like “In today’s world…” — go straight to the concept.
  • Increase length with new dimensions (features, working, examples, limitations), never with padding.
Golden rule: marks determine depth, the question type determines structure, the source determines terminology — and only academically relevant sections belong in the answer.

Q1

Which method is used for giving a proper format to the output extracted by the query?

A.format()
B.print()
C.justify()
D.pretty()
✓ Correct Answer: D. pretty()
Explanation: pretty() formats the query output into a readable, indented form.
Q2

Which statement is true about the $dirty flag?

A.$dirty flag is used to state that the value has been changed.
B.$dirty flag is used to state that the form has invalid data.
C.Both of the mentioned.
D.None of the mentioned.
✓ Correct Answer: A. $dirty flag is used to state that the value has been changed.
Explanation: $dirty becomes true once the user has changed the input value (it does not indicate invalid data).

Q1

What shapes are commonly discussed in Lilavati's geometry?

DefinitionLilavati is a celebrated treatise on arithmetic and geometry written by the Indian mathematician Bhaskaracharya II (Bhāskara II) in Sanskrit, named after his daughter Lilavati.
Geometry discussed in Lilavati
•Properties of triangles, circles, quadrilaterals.
•Secure now: area/volume of basic shapes.
•Problems on mensuration — perimeter, area, volume.
•Practical word-problems involving shapes and measurements.
Key facts
•Author: Bhāskara II (Bhaskaracharya).
•Language: originally written in Sanskrit.
•Part of his main work Siddhanta Shiromani.
•Covers arithmetic, algebra and geometry.
Q2

What is Beej-Ganita in Indian mathematics?

DefinitionBeej-Ganita (Bījagaṇita) is Bhāskara II's treatise on algebra — literally "seed mathematics" (beej = seed/root, ganita = mathematics). It is the second part of the Siddhanta Shiromani.
Meaning
•The word beej means *seed* (or root/unknown quantity).
•It deals with equations, unknowns and their solutions.
•Written in Sanskrit verses.
Significance
It systematised Indian algebra — solution of linear and quadratic equations, and the concept of zeros/negative numbers.
Q3

Explain ngOnInit and ngOnChanges.

DefinitionngOnInit runs once after a component is created (used for initialization logic); ngOnChanges runs when an @Input() value changes.
ngOnInit
•Called once after the first ngOnChanges.
•Best place to load initial data / call services.
ngOnChanges
•Called whenever a bound @Input property changes.
•Receives a SimpleChanges object with previous and current values.
Example (Angular)
CodengOnInit() { this.loadData(); } // once ngOnChanges(c){ if(c.id) this.reload(); } // on input change
Q4

Write MongoDB query to: remove all the documents from a collection; delete a collection.

DefinitionUse deleteMany({}) to remove all documents (empty condition) and drop() to delete the collection itself.
Queries
Codedb.EMPL.deleteMany({}) // remove all documents db.EMPL.drop() // delete the collection db.dropDatabase() // delete the whole database
deleteMany({}) keeps the collection structure; drop() removes the collection and its indexes completely.
Q5★ Important

What are props in React?

DefinitionProps (short for properties) are read-only values passed from a parent to a child component to make it reusable and dynamic.
Example
Codefunction Welcome(props){ return <h1>Hello {props.name}</h1>; } <Welcome name="Rahul" /> // renders: Hello Rahul
•Props flow one-way — parent to child.
•They are read-only (immutable) — cannot be changed by the child.
•Make components reusable with different data.
